checks_passed: All ten pinned raw files match manifest byte sizes and MD5 values, including the README and all nine longitudinal CSVs.
All 3,828 CSV rows contain exactly 41 finite numeric fields with no missing tokens; every file starts at t=0 and every within-file time increment is 0.025 s within the frozen 1e-9 s tolerance.

The creator-designated longitudinal partition is exactly seven training maneuvers and two validation maneuvers, with row order preserved and lag, recursive, and ACF state reset at every file boundary.

The frozen protocol precommits raw-unit preprocessing, ARX/AR order, one-sample input lag, scoring rules, aggregation, residual diagnostics, and decision rules before validation arrays are parsed; the script writes the checksummed training checkpoint before loading validation arrays and performs no validation tuning.

The ARX(2,1,1) implementation uses design rows [q[n-1], q[n-2], u[n-1], 1], target q[n], equation q_hat[n]=c+a1 q[n-1]+a2 q[n-2]+b1 u[n-1], and unweighted float64 numpy.linalg.lstsq(X,y,rcond=None) on 2,936 training rows; an independent solve reproduces all four coefficients exactly.

The matched-order input-free AR(2) baseline uses design rows [q[n-1], q[n-2], 1], the same 2,936 training targets, and the same least-squares convention; an independent solve reproduces all three coefficients exactly.

For each validation maneuver, one-step prediction uses measured q[n-1] and q[n-2], free run is initialized with the two measured within-file seeds q[0] and q[1], both modes score n=2 through L-1, and residual/error sign is measured minus predicted.

Independent reconstruction from the raw CSVs reproduces every derived prediction, residual, per-file RMSE/NRMSE, equal-maneuver macro metric, sample-pooled secondary RMSE, and NRMSE effect size with zero observed float64 difference.

The ARX homogeneous characteristic equation r^2-a1*r-a2=0 and its conjugate roots 0.8710731386675423 +/- 0.2640202360405933j are sign-consistent; both magnitudes equal 0.9102060744397689 and are strictly inside the unit circle.

The one-step ARX residual ACF is mean-centered and computed separately per maneuver for lags 1 through 20 without cross-file pairs; all values, +/-1.96/sqrt(M) descriptive bands, crossing lists, and equal-file macro ACF reproduce exactly, and the wording correctly treats crossings as diagnostic flags rather than a formal whiteness test.

Derived predictions retain only split/maneuver identity, sample/time, elevator, pitch rate, predictions, and residuals; they contain no GPS or location values, while the unmodified raw source remains checksum-pinned.
Protocol, script, source manifest, provenance, training checkpoint, validation summary, prediction CSV, and artifact-set hashes are internally consistent with the build manifest.

Two isolated full builds using the pinned NumPy 2.3.2 environment produced identical files and artifact-set SHA-256 7aee6d229999e99ff4ce8bdedb9f599c38f696adf3dc0165f6a322f976b0de82; all generated payloads also match the committed artifacts byte-for-byte.

The updated research brief and course.yaml claims match the generated evidence: ARX is strictly better than AR(2) in both modes on both validation maneuvers, equal-maneuver macro NRMSE improves by 12.0% one-step and 60.3% free-run, recurrence roots are stable, residual ACF remains structured, and the supported scope is ordinary-flight Skywalker X8 prediction rather than perching, stall, actuator-delay, or invariant-aircraft identification.

recompute.environment: Python >=3.12 with numpy==2.3.2 via the script's inline dependency declaration
